hook: Squeeze an instant cold pack and it turns icy in seconds: ammonium nitrate is dissolving and soaking up heat. Squeeze a hot pack and calcium chloride dissolves and gets warm. Both salts dissolve on their own. Free energy explains how two opposite heat effects can both lead to dissolving.

prereq.q: In water, which end of each water molecule points toward a cation?
options: The oxygen end, which is partly negative
A hydrogen end, which is partly positive
Neither: water does not attract ions
prereq.why: Opposite partial charges attract: δ− oxygen toward the cation.

prereq.q: A process has ΔH° > 0 and ΔS° > 0. When is it favored?
prereq.why: ΔG° = ΔH° − TΔS° becomes negative once TΔS° > ΔH°.

figure.caption: Dissolving: pulling ions apart and pushing water apart absorb energy; water surrounding the ions releases energy. The small difference is ΔH°soln.

chain.cause: Ions must be pulled apart and water molecules pushed apart
chain.effect: these steps absorb energy (Coulombic attractions and hydrogen bonds are overcome)

chain.cause: Water then surrounds each ion through ion-dipole attractions
chain.effect: this step releases energy, and the balance of the three steps is ΔH°soln

chain.cause: The ions spread out, but water molecules are held in place around them
chain.effect: ΔS°soln is usually positive, but can be negative for small, highly charged ions
a solid dissolves readily when ΔG°soln < 0, whether it is driven by ΔH° or by ΔS°

ideas: Dissolving = separate the solute particles (absorbs energy) + separate the solvent particles (absorbs) + form solute-solvent attractions (releases).
ΔH°soln is the small difference between large numbers, so it can be positive (cold pack) or negative (hot pack).
ΔS°soln is usually positive (ions disperse), but small, highly charged ions order the water around them and can make it negative.
A solid dissolves readily when ΔG°soln = ΔH°soln − TΔS°soln < 0; ΔG°soln = −RT ln Ksp links it to solubility.

misconception.wrong: A salt dissolves only if dissolving releases heat, because favored processes are exothermic.
misconception.right: Many salts dissolve endothermically (ammonium nitrate cools the water). They dissolve because the ions spreading out makes ΔS°soln large enough that TΔS° > ΔH°, so ΔG°soln < 0.

summary: Dissolving a solid absorbs energy to separate solute and solvent particles and releases energy as solute-solvent attractions form. The balance, ΔH°soln, can have either sign. ΔS°soln is usually positive but can be negative when water is ordered around small, highly charged ions. The solid dissolves readily when ΔG°soln < 0.
